independence: Inspected only the supplied packet and pinned raw HTML. No implementation, prior reviews, seals, or external sources were read. Acceptance concerns source fidelity, scope, dependency topology and mathematically valid proof obligations; it does not certify any formal implementation.
summary: All 50 nodes, 34 hyperedges and 5 exclusions accepted at the declared source/background-obligation granularity. The selected compact-prefactor route and optional source-sharp route each suffice for both joint absolute product integrability statements. Ex58 is an equality of signed Haar averages, and the two Fubini swaps, Gaussian integral and full B6 cancellation yield precisely Eq21.

The displayed operations are continuous or Borel in finite dimensional coordinates. Haar probability and sigma-finite Euclidean volume provide the product-measure setting. This is a genuine background proof obligation.
The source explicitly uses |det(O)|=1 in A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.3; full orthogonality implies det(O)=+1 or -1.

The lower quadratic-form bound applies to any x and to the axis vector of equal norm, implies positive determinant, and lambda >= 0 implies 0 < h_lambda <= 1. Correct background consequences.
Ex58 asserts equality of signed Haar averages for every x. The packet correctly avoids claiming equality of original and radial integrands for each fixed O.

A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.1 explicitly gives conjugation invariance, determinant preservation, precision covariance and p_(QOQ^T)(Qx)=p_O(x). Their literal-function versions follow from the displayed precision formula; axis transport completes the argument.

The upper spectral bound gives det A <= kappa^n and hence sqrt(det A)/(2pi)^(n/2) <= (kappa/(2pi))^(n/2). The positive-base real-power normalization is necessary and correctly identified as background.
Ex59 literally bounds the radial h_lambda(x)p_O(||x||e1) by (kappa/(2pi))^(n/2) exp(-||x||^2/2). The recorded constant and absence of an extra lambda factor are correct.
The identical bound for p_O(x) follows from the same determinant and lower quadratic-form bounds. It is correctly marked a derived extension rather than quoted as Ex59.

O(n) is a closed bounded subset of finite-dimensional matrix space, hence compact. The explicit determinant/sqrt/constant prefactor is continuous; its image has a finite upper bound C, which may be chosen nonnegative. This is a sufficient alternative, not the source sharp estimate.
Using |det O|=1, nonnegative prefactor, h_lambda <= 1 and the lower quadratic-form bound gives the same C exp(-||x||^2/2) envelope for both original and axis-radial integrands.

For finite nonnegative C the Euclidean Gaussian envelope is integrable, e.g. by one-dimensional Gaussian integration and finite products. Its group-independent product extension has the same integral because Haar mass is one.

Correct target: actual absolute product-measure integrability for both original and radial functions. Separate or merely iterated integrability alone would not satisfy this node; either complete domination route supplies the stronger claim.

U <= 1 and kappa-1 >= 0 give a(O) >= 2+4lambda >= 2, including lambda=0, exactly the lower bound used after Ex60.
Substitution of the axial quadratic form and h_lambda combines the exponent into -[kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U]||x||^2/4. The determinant sign and normalization are unchanged.
Correct target transported from the radial member of joint_l1 using the pointwise radial_g_algebra identity, not using an incorrect f=g assertion.

On [-1,1], a(u) >= 2+4lambda > 0. The reciprocal real power is continuous and bounded, so the Haar weighted expectations are integrable. A Borel extension or the globally defined real-power expression can be used outside the support.
Lemma B.6/Equation 15 explicitly assumes Borel h with E|h(U)| finite and states exactly the sign, beta^(n-1), 2^n denominator and linear numerator recorded in the packet.
This is precisely B6 applied to h(u)=a(u)^(-n/2). The support bound and boundedness justify its integrability without a uniform-sphere law.

The conjunction of original product L1, radial g product L1 and the exact scalar formula is a faithful scoped target. Acceptance is of this statement and dependency plan, not a claim that its formal proof has been completed.
Finite-dimensional Euclidean orthogonal transformations take x to ||x||e1 for nonzero x; zero is fixed and handled directly. This uses no distribution on a sphere.

The source explicitly argues invertibility throughout the interval, positivity at t=0 and positivity throughout by continuity. The provider must use determinant continuity, not measurability alone.

A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.3 explicitly uses |det O_(S,S)|<=1 to justify finiteness under the B6 assumption E|h(U)| finite. The principal-minor bound follows from orthogonal matrix compression/operator norm or Hadamard.
